subject: Any thoughts on implementing menus in shiny?

messages.author: 889de486273d901d
messages.subject: Any thoughts on implementing menus in shiny?
parts:
I've been playing with implementing dropdown menus in shiny but I've run into a snag.
In bootstrap menus are implemented as a <div> enclosing a <ul> tag enclosing a series of <li><a></a></li> tags.

<div class="dropdown btn-group navicon" type="navicon">
   <a class="btn btn-small dropdown-toggle" data-toggle="dropdown" href="#">
   <img src="navicon.svg"/>
   </a>
   <ul class="dropButton dropdown-menu " id="printmenu1">
      <li data-choice="print">
         <a href="#">Print chart</a>
      </li>
      <li data-choice="png">
         <a  href="#">Download PNG image</a>
      </li>
      <li data-choice="pdf">
         <a  href="#">Download PDF document</a>
      </li>
   </ul>
</div>
The question is how to hook that control up to Shiny?  I have so far chosen to put the id on the <ul> tag and have it catch click messages bubbling up from the <li> elements.  That means I have one control in Shiny per menu,

    observe({
        selection = input$printmenu1
        if (is.null(selection))
            return()
        message("Inside printmenu observer")
        if (selection == "print") {
            message(" invoke print")
        } else if (selection == "png") {
            message(" invoke png")
        } else if (selection == "pdf") {
            message(" invoke pdf")
        } else {
            message(paste0(" unknown printmenu command - ", selection) )
        }
    })

The problem is if the user selects the same menu item again, Shiny doesn't get any message.  It is filtered out at about line 307 of shiny.js,

    this.setInput = function(name, value) {
      var jsonValue = JSON.stringify(value);
      if (this.lastSentValues[name] === jsonValue)
        return;

This filter is in place to prevent multiple notifications of identical values, and works well for controls like selectInput, but doesn't work well with menus and action buttons which want to trigger every time that are activated.   Action buttons have a hack to get around this by simply incrementing the value returned.

So what is the right thing to do here?   Should I turn every item in the menu into its own Shiny control, as if they were a series of action buttons?  Or should append a monotonically increasing number to the value of this menu control so you would get back values like "png-1", "png-2", "png-3"?  I'm strongly leaning towards keeping a single control per menu because that feel most natural to me.

- chris

messages.author: 889de486273d901d
messages.subject: Re: Any thoughts on implementing menus in shiny?
parts:
Thank you for that pointer - Vincent's app has lots of little gems that I am learning from.   He has efficiently solved the problem I was asking about earlier by explicitly clearing menus in the click callback.  No need to update to a later version of bootstrap.  (I'll update the earlier thread with this info.)

However he has not solved the problem I am asking about in this thread.   The dropdown menus on his navbar do a single notification and then do nothing if you select the same item again - the same way every control except actionButton works.   That is fine for a navbar but is not what you want for a dropdown menu that should trigger an action each time an item is selected.   

However his inputBinding code is much cleaner than what I was doing so I'll incorporate that.  Then I'll just add an integer to values sent back through Shiny from the menu, just like actionButton does, and strip it off in the reactive function.
